titulo: Real-to-sim: bringing the real world into the simulator
lead: So far the path has gone from the simulator to the robot. The reverse path exists too: photograph the real place and build a twin where the robot trains and is tested first. In this lesson you run the twin from the robotica-real2sim project (an arm, not a humanoid) in the course venv and prove a plan in the physics, and you see where this stands for humanoids in 2026.
objetivo: run the robotica-real2sim twin in the course venv and prove a plan in the physics before the robot, counting the objects in the scene.

aprende.t: The flow: photo → scene → twin → episodes → proof
The robotica-real2sim twin running with the Menagerie from your bench
A plan approved in 19 of 20 variations in the physics
Real-to-sim for humanoids in 2026: vendor demo, reported

hero_alt: A real table with a red cube, a blue can, a tennis ball, and a tray, photographed by a phone on a tripod, with the simulated twin on a monitor beside it.

secoes.titulo: From the real place to the twin
secoes.sub: Click each block. This is the robotica-real2sim flow.

nos.detalhe: A photo of the table, with an A4 sheet as a ruler. In the project, a vision model reads the photo; this course doesn't run that step (it calls a model) and starts from the scene already prepared.
Objects, sizes and positions in meters. Whatever is wrong here (a tray bigger than the real one) becomes a twin (digital twin) error.
The scene becomes MJCF with the Franka Panda arm from Menagerie. Here the twin (digital twin) is rendered so you can compare it with the photo.
The plan runs 20 times with varied positions and sizes. It only goes to the robot if it passes at 90% or more: the same logic as the gate in lesson 6.

secoes.legenda: Real-to-sim is the subject of robotica-real2sim. Here it runs and is tied to the ladder: a twin (digital twin) of the place is one more step before the floor.

secoes.sub: Status as of Oct 2026, according to the program's research. Click each item.

texto: Niantic Spatial, Flexion and NVIDIA showed a scene scanned by camera turning into Gaussian splatting in Isaac Sim, with a humanoid navigation policy trained there and taken to the robot with no tuning. This is vendor material, not a paper with measurements.

Berkeley, ETH and Amazon FAR use 3DGS as a renderer inside a vectorized simulator, at 100k+ steps per second (arXiv 2510.15352). Also with no measured sim-to-real on a humanoid as of Oct 2026, according to the research.
What already makes it into day-to-day work is simpler: measuring the floor and the friction, weighing the robot, scanning steps and obstacles for the terrain curriculum (course 1).

A twin (digital twin) is only as good as the measurement that feeds it. The real2sim project measured this: different vision models got the tray size wrong, and the proof only approves what passes in the worst case.

secoes.titulo: Run the twin and the proof
secoes.sub: Adds the Panda to the bench's Menagerie sparse-checkout, pins robotica-real2sim to the tested commit and points its vendor/menagerie to yours.

blocos.conteudo:
F=${FTH:-$HOME/fth}; cd $F && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -q pillow imageio
git -C mujoco_menagerie sparse-checkout add franka_emika_panda
[ -d robotica-real2sim ] || git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/robotica-real2sim
git -C robotica-real2sim checkout -q 3a08537 && mkdir -p robotica-real2sim/vendor
ln -sfn $F/mujoco_menagerie robotica-real2sim/vendor/menagerie
cd robotica-real2sim && python3 r2s.py ver exemplos/mesa-foto/cena.json $F/gemeo.png --camera cima
python3 $F/sim2real/kit/gemeo.py exemplos/mesa-foto/cena.json $F/gemeo.png

F=${FTH:-$HOME/fth}; cd $F/robotica-real2sim && . $F/.venv/bin/activate
python3 r2s.py provar exemplos/mesa-foto/cena.json resultados/mesa-foto/plano.json -n 20 | tail -3

abas.rot: Common error: no GPU to render with
abas.html:
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'glGetError'

r2s.py renders on the GPU (MUJOCO_GL=egl). Without a GPU, switch to osmesa, but the OSMesa library must be installed; without it, you get the error above. Counting objects doesn't depend on rendering: gemeo.py reads cena.json.

exercicios.texto: For a G1 that will walk down a factory corridor, list three measurements of the real place that you would bring into the simulator before the ladder in lesson 8.
exercicios.pronto: three items with what to measure and with which instrument (e.g., floor friction with an inclined plane; step height with a tape measure).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What does real-to-sim do that sim-to-real does not?
opcoes: It trains the policy directly on the robot, without a simulator.
It brings the real place into the simulator before the test.
It replaces randomization with a single exact measurement of the real place.
It makes the sim2sim gate unnecessary.
perguntas.explica: It's the opposite direction: measure the world and build the twin. Then the way back (sim-to-real) still uses randomization, the gate, and the ladder.

perguntas.p: As of Oct 2026, real-to-sim with Gaussian splatting for humanoids is:
opcoes: Required by regulation before you power on the robot.
Vendor demo (reported), no sim-to-real measured in a paper.
Impossible, because splatting doesn't run on a GPU.
perguntas.explica: The course research found demos (Niantic/Flexion/NVIDIA) and GaussGym, but no published sim-to-real measurement for a humanoid. Stated as reported.

perguntas.p: Without a GPU, r2s.py ver gives an OpenGL error. How do you go on?
opcoes: Switch to MUJOCO_GL=osmesa with OSMesa installed.
Delete cena.json and generate another one.
Use unitree_mujoco in place of the desk twin, which doesn't render.
perguntas.explica: The rendering is just the image. With OSMesa it runs on the CPU; the object count and the physics test don't even need rendering.

itens.texto: Photo, scene, twin, and a physics test before the robot.
The example plan passes 19 of 20 variations.
A splatting twin (digital twin) for humanoids is still a vendor demo (reported); measuring the place is already routine.
